base_instruction: You are a helpful office party planning assistant. Help the user plan food and drinks for their team's holiday party by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and any logistics. When the user asks you to evaluate specific menu items, check each item against every active attendee's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and constraint updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, we're planning our office holiday party for next Thursday and I'm in charge of the food. Can you help me figure out what to order?

flow_info.value: Five of us confirmed so far: me, Rachel, Dev, Marcus, and Tina
Dev was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
Marcus had a peanut allergy incident at last year's party, had to use his EpiPen
Company gave us $300 for catering, about 8-10 people expected total
Tina just told me she's going on vacation early, flying out Wednesday night, so she won't be there
Tina asked if I could save her a box of whatever desserts we get though
Marcus told me he did allergy testing last month and turns out he's outgrown the peanut allergy completely, doctor cleared him
Marcus wants to bring his wife Priya to the party
Oh and our new intern Sam is coming too, started last week
Catering menu options I'm looking at: smoked salmon platter, penne pasta with vodka sauce, Thai chicken satay with peanut sauce, flourless chocolate cake, fruit and cheese board, mulled wine

constraints.value: Cannot eat raw or smoked fish, cannot drink alcohol
inference_chain: Seven months pregnant → pregnancy dietary restrictions apply

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — no wheat, barley, rye, or products containing them
constraints.surface_form: Dev was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye
No gluten → no regular pasta, bread, most baked goods unless explicitly gluten-free

constraints.value: Cannot eat tree nuts — almonds, cashews, walnuts, pistachios, etc.
constraints.surface_form: Tina carries an EpiPen for tree nuts, she's mentioned it a few times at lunch
inference_chain: Carries EpiPen for tree nuts → severe tree nut allergy
Tree nut allergy → cannot eat almonds, cashews, walnuts, pistachios, etc.

constraints.value: Cannot have high-sugar foods without careful portion control, needs low-glycemic options available
constraints.surface_form: Sam mentioned on his first day that he wears an insulin pump, been Type 1 since he was a kid
inference_chain: Type 1 diabetic → must manage carbohydrate/sugar intake carefully
Party context → needs low-sugar or portionable options available

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables (onion, garlic, potatoes)
constraints.surface_form: Marcus mentioned his wife Priya is Jain, very observant about it
inference_chain: Jain vegetarian → no meat, no fish, no eggs
Observant Jain → also no root vegetables (onion, garlic, potatoes)

hidden_state.value: You are an office worker planning your team's holiday party food. You will introduce your colleagues and their backgrounds across several turns. People will join and leave the guest list. A new intern with diabetes joins late. At the end, you will share a catering menu and ask if there are any issues — you must NOT hint at what the problems are or which constraints to check.

You are a calm, friendly office party planner. You always refer to your colleagues by name in third person (e.g. 'Rachel told me...', 'Marcus said...'). You never express frustration or impatience, even when the guest list keeps changing. You treat each update as normal office coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for colleague updates

aims.description: OK so I found a catering company with good reviews. Here's what I'm thinking of ordering: smoked salmon platter, penne pasta with vodka sauce, Thai chicken satay with peanut sauce, flourless chocolate cake, fruit and cheese board, and mulled wine. Any issues?
aims.success_criteria: Agent identifies: smoked salmon problematic for Rachel (pregnant, no smoked fish) and Priya (Jain, no fish); penne pasta problematic for Dev (celiac, contains gluten) and Priya (likely contains garlic/onion); Thai chicken satay problematic for Priya (Jain, no meat) but peanut sauce is NOW FINE (Marcus outgrew allergy); flourless chocolate cake is fine for the party table but must check for tree nuts before saving for Tina; fruit and cheese board is fine for most; mulled wine problematic for Rachel (pregnant, no alcohol)
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 6 menu items against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Smoked salmon platter: problematic for Rachel (pregnant — smoked fish carries listeria risk) and Priya (Jain — no fish). Penne pasta with vodka sauce: problematic for Dev (celiac — penne is wheat pasta, contains gluten) and Priya (vodka sauce typically contains garlic/onion — Jain restriction on root vegetables). Thai chicken satay with peanut sauce: problematic for Priya (Jain — no meat/chicken); peanut sauce is fine because Marcus outgrew his peanut allergy. Flourless chocolate cake: fine for the party table, but need to verify it doesn't contain tree nuts before saving a box for Tina (tree nut allergy still applies to her saved desserts); also Sam (Type 1 diabetic) needs portion awareness but cake can still be served. Fruit and cheese board: generally fine for everyone at the table. Mulled wine: problematic for Rachel (pregnant — no alcohol).
required_elements: Smoked salmon platter is problematic for Rachel because she is pregnant and smoked fish poses listeria risk
Smoked salmon platter is problematic for Priya because she is Jain and cannot eat fish
Penne pasta with vodka sauce is problematic for Dev because he has celiac disease and penne contains gluten
Penne pasta with vodka sauce is problematic for Priya because vodka sauce typically contains garlic and/or onion which are root vegetables forbidden in Jain diet
Thai chicken satay is problematic for Priya because she is Jain and cannot eat meat
Peanut sauce is fine — Marcus outgrew his peanut allergy, doctor cleared him
Flourless chocolate cake needs to be checked for tree nuts before saving for Tina's box, since her tree nut allergy still applies to saved desserts
Mulled wine is problematic for Rachel because she is pregnant and cannot have alcohol
Sam as Type 1 diabetic should be noted regarding high-sugar items like cake, but items can still be served with awareness
forbidden_elements: Flagging peanut sauce as a problem for Marcus (he outgrew the allergy, doctor cleared him)
Flagging tree nuts as a problem for the party table (Tina is not attending the party itself)
Saying Priya cannot eat cheese (Jain diet restricts meat/fish/eggs/root vegetables, not dairy)
Saying Sam cannot have any cake or sugar at all (Type 1 diabetics manage intake, not eliminate it entirely)
Flagging any item for Tina as if she is attending the party in person
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across 9 conversational turns. The agent must track: (1) Rachel is pregnant → no smoked fish, no alcohol (inferential chain), (2) Dev has celiac → no gluten (inferential), (3) Marcus's peanut allergy is REMOVED mid-conversation (outgrown, doctor cleared), (4) Tina EXITS the party but wants desserts saved (tree nut allergy scope changes from party table to saved desserts only), (5) Priya JOINS late as a Jain → no meat, fish, eggs, root vegetables including garlic and onion (inferential, high-constraint late-joiner), (6) Sam JOINS late as Type 1 diabetic → needs sugar awareness but not elimination (inferential, late-joiner). At probe time, the agent must apply CURRENT constraint state: Rachel=pregnant (no smoked fish, no alcohol), Dev=celiac (no gluten), Priya=Jain (no meat/fish/eggs/root vegetables), Sam=Type 1 diabetic (sugar awareness), Tina=tree nut allergy (desserts saved for her only). Marcus has NO restrictions. The peanut sauce trap tests whether the agent correctly removes Marcus's former constraint. The flourless chocolate cake tests scope distinction (fine for table, must check for Tina's box). The fruit and cheese board tests over-generalization (Jain does not restrict dairy).

mechanism: Late-joiner with high-constraint: new person with strict needs arrives late
